items.title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
items.summary: DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice.

items.title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
items.summary: (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms.

items.title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
items.summary: Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.

items.title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
items.summary: Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

items.title: Calling species 'invasive'—and culling them—isn't done lightly. But it matters to Australia's threatened species
items.summary: It may sound abstract, but distinctions between "native," "introduced" or "invasive" species can often be life or death. Species considered invasive in Australia—such as European rabbits and feral pigs—are often culled, while most native animals are generally left alone.
